name: GraphIC: A Graph-Based In-Context Example Retrieval Model for Multi-Step Reasoning
venue: arXiv 2410.02203 (Oct 2024); published at AAAI 2026 (The Fortieth AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence, AAAI-26, pp. 30753-30761, AAAI Press, 2026)
authors_affiliation: Jiale Fu, Jiaming Fan, Xu Yang (corresponding) - Southeast University, PALM Lab / Key Laboratory of New Generation Artificial Intelligence Technology and Its Interdisciplinary Applications (Southeast University), Ministry of Education, China; Yaqing Wang (corresponding) - Beijing Institute of Mathematical Sciences and Applications (BIMSA); Simeng Han - Stanford University (Yale University in arXiv v1). Lead author Jiale Fu is a Master's student at Southeast University.
task_domain: Multi-step reasoning: QA / mathematical reasoning, code generation, and logical reasoning (in-context demonstration example retrieval for LLM ICL).
problem_setting: Offline, single-LLM in-context learning (ICL) setting. Given a fixed candidate pool of training examples with ground-truth chain-of-thought reasoning, the method selects k demonstration examples (in-context examples, ICEs) for each test query to be placed in the prompt. No model parameter updates; the method itself is training-free (no retriever training). Supervision: candidate examples have ground-truth reasoning processes used to build thought graphs; queries have no ground truth so a pseudo reasoning process is generated by the LLM. Standard 8-shot CoT prompting setting.
what_is_retrieved: Demonstrations (in-context examples / ICEs) for ICL, i.e. (problem, chain-of-thought solution) demonstration pairs, selected via their thought-graph representations.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus: a fixed training/candidate example set is the retrievable store; it does not grow during deployment. Thought graphs and reasoning-pattern parameters for all candidates are precomputed offline.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k ranking: GraphIC scores each candidate's reasoning-pattern applicability to the query thought graph and selects the top-k (e.g. 8-shot) examples. No notion of recovering a complete minimal set or variable/precision-driven size.
cbr_cycle_coverage: Retrieve only (Retrieve: yes; Reuse: examples are inserted verbatim as ICL exemplars, not adapted; Revise: no; Retain: no). Not framed as CBR.
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The paper does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; it is framed as in-context example retrieval / graph-based reasoning, drawing on cognitive science (Friston) and graph-of-thought / tree-of-thought reasoning work.
retrieval_unit: Single demonstration (problem-solution example), represented as a thought graph - a directed, node-attributed graph whose nodes are reasoning steps (math operations / code snippets / intermediate conclusions, embedded via BERT) and edges encode step dependencies.
index_source: Static corpus, offline-induced. Thought graphs for all N candidate examples are constructed offline from their ground-truth reasoning, and a reasoning-pattern parameter W_i is precomputed for each during a preparation stage.
index_structure_topology: Per-item dependency GRAPH (thought graph) plus a flat collection of per-candidate reasoning-pattern parameters; retrieval is a flat scan computing a graph-similarity score of each candidate's reasoning pattern against the query thought graph (no clustering/hierarchy over the store).
retriever_type: LLM-as-retriever (hybrid): an LLM generates a Formalized Reasoning Representation (FRR) / pseudo reasoning that is rule-parsed into a thought graph; node attributes use a dense BERT embedding model; retrieval is a custom graph-similarity metric (not BM25/standard dense cosine).
retriever_learning_signal: None (training-free / off-the-shelf). No retriever training. The reasoning-pattern parameter W per graph is obtained by a closed-form optimization (rank-1 SVD solution maximizing a bilinear applicability objective under a Frobenius-norm constraint), not learned from similarity labels, LM feedback, or RL.
query_construction: For a query (which lacks ground-truth reasoning), the LLM generates a pseudo natural-language reasoning process, which is formalized into an FRR and rule-parsed into a query thought graph G^q; correctness of the pseudo reasoning is not required (robust to inaccuracies). Candidate keys are thought graphs built from their ground-truth CoT.
query_granularity: Task-level (one-shot at t=0): a single thought graph is built per query before answering and used for a single retrieval call.
when_to_retrieve: One-shot: retrieval happens once per query before generation; the selected k ICEs are fixed for the whole answer.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule: retrieve once per query at prompt-construction time (no confidence/uncertainty/iterative trigger).
reranking: No separate reranking stage; the proposed asymmetric reasoning-pattern applicability metric A(W_i; G^q) is itself the single scoring/ranking function, and top-k are taken directly.
retrieved_context_refinement: None (no post-retrieval rerank/compression/distillation). Selected examples are inserted directly. (The FRR/thought-graph construction acts as a representation-level filter of shallow semantics, but this happens before similarity computation, not as post-retrieval refinement.)
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation: the top-k retrieved demonstrations are inserted verbatim as in-context exemplars in the chain-of-thought prompt; the LLM then answers the query.
planning_integration: One-shot exemplars at plan/answer time: retrieved demonstrations are placed in the prompt before a single CoT generation. No interleaving with planning, no tree/MCTS search, no per-step retrieval.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-answer: a single retrieval feeds the entire CoT generation for the query (retrieval is not interleaved per reasoning step).
retrieved_item_representation: Raw demonstration (original problem + ground-truth chain-of-thought) injected as text exemplars. The thought-graph / FRR representation is used internally for retrieval scoring, not injected into the prompt.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Single demonstration (raw problem-CoT example). Internally matched via a distilled reasoning-structure representation (thought graph) but the injected unit is a full demonstration.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Representation-level filtering plus robustness to imperfect query reasoning: FRR / thought graphs filter out shallow semantic noise and preserve reasoning structure, reducing distractor selection; the query's pseudo reasoning need not be correct (partially-correct reasoning still aids retrieval), so GraphIC stays accurate even with incorrect generated reasoning. No retriever-aware training or self-reflection relevance evaluator.
memory_type: graph (per-item thought graphs over a static candidate store); no episodic/skill/workflow memory that grows.
write_back: False - no experiences/cases are written back; the candidate store and its thought graphs are fixed (computed once offline).
online_growth: No - the retrievable store does not grow during deployment/test-time; it is frozen after offline induction.
failure_experience_usage: Not used as a memory mechanism. Note: success-only candidates (ground-truth correct CoT) form the store; failed solutions are not stored or retrieved. (The query's own possibly-incorrect pseudo reasoning is used only transiently for retrieval, not stored.)
memory_evolution_update: N/A (append-only is not applicable; the store is static and entries are never mutated).
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No - retrieval is not a learned/RL policy. It is a fixed (training-free) top-k selection using a closed-form-computed reasoning-pattern similarity metric; W is solved analytically per graph, not learned as a policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No - single-LLM, private static candidate set; no cross-agent or cross-framework memory sharing.
benchmarks: GSM8K (math), AQUA / AQuA-RAT (math), MBPP (code generation), ProofWriter (logical reasoning).
benchmark_family: QA / math reasoning (GSM8K, AQUA), code (MBPP), and logical reasoning (ProofWriter). Multi-step reasoning benchmarks for ICL demonstration selection.
baselines: 10 baselines: 6 training-free (Random, BM25, BERT dense retriever, Complex-CoT, Auto-CoT, Skill-kNN) and 4 training-based (EPR, CEIL, DQ-LoRe, GistScore).
key_metrics: Answer accuracy for GSM8K, AQUA, ProofWriter; pass@1 for MBPP; reported as per-dataset and average across the 4 datasets. Also a qualitative score-matrix vs ground-truth 'improve matrix' alignment analysis.
headline_result: GraphIC (training-free) outperforms all 10 baselines: average accuracy 78.26% with GPT-4o-mini and 70.83% with Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (8-shot), beating the best training-free baseline by 2.57%/4.29% and the best training-based baseline by 1.18%/2.50% respectively; largest gains on AQUA (+3.47% GPT-4o-mini, +7.64% Llama-3 over baselines).
ablations: Component ablation (Llama-3, 4 datasets): Text (BERT) -> FRR (text-embedding of FRR) -> Graph (graph embedding via cosine, Eq.5) -> +B (backtracking/traceback matrix) -> +S (asymmetric reasoning-pattern similarity) -> +B+S (full GraphIC). FRR filtering lifts GSM8K 74.15->78.31 and ProofWriter 73.75->82.50; graph structure lifts AQUA 50.78->54.72; full reasoning-aware similarity lifts AQUA 54.72->57.48. Backtracking and the asymmetric similarity each add gains, with the best results when all components combined. Also: k-shot analysis (1/2/4/8 shots) showing GraphIC improves steadily with k while baselines (DQ-LoRe, Complex-CoT) degrade; asymmetry analysis showing GraphIC's score matrix aligns best with the ground-truth improve matrix.
evaluation_decoupling: Partially: primarily end-to-end task accuracy/pass@1. No standard Recall@k/nDCG retrieval metrics, but it does report a separate retrieval-quality-style analysis (alignment of each method's score matrix with a ground-truth 'improve matrix' built from one-shot solve probabilities), decoupling retrieval-quality alignment from final task accuracy.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome (final answer accuracy / pass@1). Some process-level analysis via the improve-matrix / score-matrix alignment, but no step-wise reasoning-faithfulness scoring.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: GraphIC is training-free (no retriever training cost) yet beats training-based methods; it does incur extra retrieval-time cost from invoking an LLM to generate FRR/pseudo reasoning per example/query (acknowledged like Skill-kNN and DQ-LoRe). Rank-1 constraint on W gives a closed-form SVD solution, avoiding expensive d x d matrix optimization (d up to 768 for BERT). No explicit latency/token-cost numbers reported in main text.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k: default 8-shot; analysis varies k in {1,2,4,8}. No explicit token budget cap; top-k by the reasoning-pattern applicability score, truncated at k.
builds_on: In-context learning / ICL example selection (EPR, CEIL, DQ-LoRe, Skill-kNN, Complex-CoT, Auto-CoT); BERT embeddings (Devlin et al.); graph-/tree-of-thought reasoning (Besta et al. Graph of Thoughts, Yao et al. Tree of Thoughts); cognitive science (Friston hierarchical inference). arXiv v1 additionally framed the model on Bayesian Networks and Personalized PageRank, later reformulated as a reasoning-pattern bilinear/rank-1 metric.
contrasts_with: Text-embedding similarity retrievers (BERT dense, BM25) that capture shallow semantics; symmetric attributed-graph embedding similarity (cosine of iteratively-aggregated graph embeddings, Eq.5); complexity/diversity heuristics (Complex-CoT, Auto-CoT); training-based retrievers (EPR, CEIL, DQ-LoRe, GistScore). GraphIC contrasts via reasoning-aware thought-graph representation and an asymmetric, sequence-aware similarity metric, while remaining training-free.
lineage: Group A (ICL demonstration retrieval): reasoning-aware / structure-aware in-context example selection for multi-step reasoning, extending text-similarity and skill/complexity-based ICE selection toward graph-based reasoning-structure matching.
